title: Cinema Cashier
statementMd:
All cinema halls in Berland are rectangles with $*K*$ rows of $*K*$ seats each, and $*K*$ is an odd number. Rows and seats are numbered from $1$ to $*K*$. For safety reasons people, who come to the box office to buy tickets, are not allowed to choose seats themselves. Formerly the choice was made by a cashier, but now this is the responsibility of a special seating program. It was found out that the large majority of Berland's inhabitants go to the cinema in order to watch a movie, that's why they want to sit as close to the hall center as possible. Moreover, a company of $*M*$ people, who come to watch a movie, want necessarily to occupy $*M*$ successive seats in one row. Let's formulate the algorithm, according to which the program chooses seats and sells tickets. As the request for $*M*$ seats comes, the program should determine the row number $*x*$ and the segment $[*y*_{*l*}, *y*_{*r*}]$ of the seats numbers in this row, where $*y*_{*r*} - *y*_{*l*} + 1 = *M*$. From all such possible variants as a final result the program should choose the one with the minimum function value of total seats remoteness from the center. Say, ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/de21a9bdfc2f66814cc5291ec42a9813f7f3b391.png) — the row and the seat numbers of the most "central" seat. Then the function value of seats remoteness from the hall center is ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/a6ae5b08ea1c4d15f150b1a9df3c925c2b9cdd51.png). If the amount of minimum function values is more than one, the program should choose the one that is closer to the screen (i.e. the row number $*x*$ is lower). If the variants are still multiple, it should choose the one with the minimum $*y*_{*l*}$. If you did not get yet, your task is to simulate the work of this program.

## Input

The first line contains two integers $*N*$ and $*K*$ ($1 ≤ *N* ≤ 1000, 1 ≤ *K* ≤ 99$) — the amount of requests and the hall size respectively. The second line contains $*N*$ space-separated integers $*M*_{*i*}$ from the range $[1, *K*]$ — requests to the program.

## Output

Output $*N*$ lines. In the $*i*$-th line output «-1» (without quotes), if it is impossible to find $*M*_{*i*}$ successive seats in one row, otherwise output three numbers $*x*, *y*_{*l*}, *y*_{*r*}$. Separate the numbers with a space.
statementZhMd:
所有伯兰德的电影院大厅都是矩形的，每个大厅有 $*K*$ 排，每排有 $*K*$ 个座位，并且 $*K*$ 是奇数。行和座位的编号均为 $1$ 到 $*K*$。出于安全原因，前来售票处购票的人不允许自行选择座位。以前座位由售票员选择，但现在这项工作由专门的座位安排程序负责。调查发现，绝大多数伯兰德居民去电影院是为了观看电影，因此他们希望尽可能坐在靠近大厅中心的位置。此外，一同前来观看电影的 $*M*$ 个人必须占据同一排中连续的 $*M*$ 个座位。

现在来描述该程序选择座位并售票的算法。当收到购买 $*M*$ 个座位的请求时，程序应确定行号 $*x*$，以及该行中的座位编号区间 $[*y*_{*l*}, *y*_{*r*}]$，其中 $*y*_{*r*} - *y*_{*l*} + 1 = *M*$。在所有可能的方案中，程序应选择使座位到大厅中心的总距离函数值最小的方案。设 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/de21a9bdfc2f66814cc5291ec42a9813f7f3b391.png) 表示最“居中”座位所在的行号和座位号。那么，座位到大厅中心的距离函数值为 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/a6ae5b08ea1c4d15f150b1a9df3c925c2b9cdd51.png)。如果函数最小值对应的方案不止一个，程序应选择离屏幕更近的方案（即行号 $*x*$ 更小的方案）。如果仍有多个方案，则选择 $*y*_{*l*}$ 最小的方案。如果你还没有理解，那么你的任务就是模拟该程序的工作过程。

## 输入格式

第一行包含两个整数 $*N*$ 和 $*K*$（$1 ≤ *N* ≤ 1000$，$1 ≤ *K* ≤ 99$），分别表示请求数量和大厅大小。第二行包含 $*N*$ 个以空格分隔的整数 $*M*_{*i*}$，每个数均属于区间 $[1, *K*]$，表示向程序提出的请求。

## 输出格式

输出 $*N*$ 行。第 $*i*$ 行中，如果无法在某一排找到连续的 $*M*_{*i*}$ 个座位，则输出「-1」（不含引号）；否则输出三个数 $*x*$、$*y*_{*l*}$、$*y*_{*r*}$。用空格分隔这些数字。
